title: Show an invoice's own page
body:
Clicking an invoice id in the table should open /invoices/<id>, which shows that invoice's customer, amount (with a dollar sign), issue date and status, and a link back to the list. An unknown id shows a not-found page.

---
_Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code)_

spec.plan:
Today the Invoice cell of each row on /invoices is plain text and there is no route under /invoices/<id>, so an invoice cannot be opened. After this change the id in every row is a next/link to /invoices/<id>; that route is a new async server component at app/invoices/[id]/page.tsx which looks the invoice up with a new pure findInvoice(id) in lib/invoices.ts and renders its customer, amount via the existing formatCurrency (so the figure carries a dollar sign, e.g. $1,180.00), issue date and status, plus a 'Back to invoices' link; when no invoice has that id it calls notFound() from next/navigation, which answers 404 and renders a new app/invoices/[id]/not-found.tsx saying the invoice was not found with the same back link.

Four decisions the builder should not re-open, each settled by the research below. (1) The lookup is a new findInvoice in lib/invoices.ts rather than filtering in the page, because lib/ is this repo's one domain module and the page must stay free of domain rules. (2) findInvoice searches the whole seeded list, NOT exportableInvoices — drafts and voids are visible in the table, so every row must open; the sent/paid rule belongs to the export and nowhere else. (3) The amount uses formatCurrency, which already exists and already yields the dollar sign and thousands separator; do not add a second formatter. (4) A small not-found.tsx is included rather than falling back to Next's built-in 404, because the built-in page is a bare framework screen with no way back to the list and nothing invoice-specific to assert on; the custom one is eleven lines and uses the same conventions as app/page.tsx.

Every new and changed source file must finish at 100% line coverage, because .factory/guardrails/coverage.json sets diff_min_pct to 80 and the runner measures diff coverage over the changed lines — a not-found.tsx with no test was measured here at 0% and pulled the whole change under the minimum. Follow the repo's conventions throughout: server components with no "use client", no inline styles (app/page.tsx has none either), @/ imports across folders and ./name.js inside a folder, and test names that say what a reader loses. Nothing else is in scope: the invoices table is not re-laid-out, no sorting or filtering is added, and the feature map is not edited (it is under .factory/definition/, which this pipeline may not change).
acceptance_checks: On http://localhost:3000/invoices, the Invoice cell of every row is a link: the INV-1002 cell is an anchor whose href is /invoices/INV-1002, and clicking it leaves the list for that URL.

http://localhost:3000/invoices/INV-1002 answers HTTP 200 and the page shows all four fields for that invoice: the customer Northwind Books, the amount $1,180.00 with the dollar sign, the issue date 2026-10-11 and the status sent.

http://localhost:3000/invoices/INV-1004 answers HTTP 200 and shows Initech Hardware, $931.00, 2026-11-01 and draft — a draft is listed in the table, so its row must open too; the sent/paid rule stays confined to the export.
The invoice page carries a link reading 'Back to invoices' whose href is /invoices, and clicking it returns to the list showing all five invoices.

http://localhost:3000/invoices/INV-9999 answers HTTP 404 and the rendered page reads 'Invoice not found' with a 'Back to invoices' link. Check this in a browser, not with curl's raw HTML: the not-found body is delivered inside a streamed Suspense template, so it is present in the response bytes but only becomes visible text once React hydrates it.
npm run build, npm test, npm run typecheck and npm run lint all still exit 0, and the build's route table lists /invoices/[id] as a dynamic (f) route.
tests_added: app/invoices/[id]/page.test.tsx — renders the page component directly with `render(await InvoicePage({ params: Promise.resolve({ id: "INV-1001" }) }))` and asserts the heading is INV-1001 and the body contains Acme Bakery, $245.00, 2026-10-02 and paid; a second case asserts the back link's href is /invoices; a third asserts an unknown id rejects, with `await expect(InvoicePage({ params: Promise.resolve({ id: "INV-9999" }) })).rejects.toThrow()`, because notFound() throws rather than returning.
app/invoices/[id]/not-found.test.tsx — renders the not-found component and asserts it says 'Invoice not found' and links back to /invoices. This test is what keeps the file off 0% coverage.

research.claim: The Invoice cell renders the bare id today, so making a row openable is a one-line change here: wrap {i.id} in a next/link anchor to `/invoices/${i.id}`. The table lists every invoice, drafts and voids included, which is why the detail route must not filter.
research.source: app/invoices/page.tsx:25 (the <td> for the id), with the unfiltered listInvoices() it maps over at app/invoices/page.tsx:23

research.claim: formatCurrency already renders cents with a dollar sign and a thousands separator from a locale-pinned Intl.NumberFormat, so 'amount (with a dollar sign)' needs no new code; its test already fixes $1,497.50 as the expected shape. Adding a second money formatter would contradict the 'one domain module' rule in fundamentals.md.

The seeded INVOICES array in lib/ is the only data source in the app, and every reader already reaches it through a pure exported function. A findInvoice(id) built on INVOICES.find is therefore the shape this repo already uses, and placing it beside listInvoices keeps the page free of domain logic.
research.source: lib/invoices.ts:11 (the readonly INVOICES array) and lib/invoices.ts:19 (listInvoices, the existing accessor)

research.claim: next/link is already how this repo links between routes, used with no wrapper and no styling, so the table cell and the back link should look the same way.

Route handlers and pages here are nested one segment deep under app/invoices/, so app/invoices/[id]/ mirrors the existing app/invoices/export/ layout rather than inventing a new top-level folder. Neither imports from another feature folder; both reach down to lib/ only.

This repo already renders server page components directly with @testing-library/react under jsdom — no router mock, no Next test harness — and that test is why app/invoices/page.tsx measures 100% line coverage today. The new page tests follow the same pattern; the async page is awaited before being handed to render().

Next is pinned at 15.5.29, where a page's params prop is a Promise. The signature `{ params: Promise<{ id: string }> }` with `const { id } = await params` was compiled by the real build and by tsc --noEmit with strict and noUncheckedIndexedAccess, both exit 0; the build's route table printed `f /invoices/[id]` (server-rendered on demand) alongside the existing static routes, so the new route does not disturb the prerendering of / and /invoices.
research.source: ran: npm ci && npm run build && npm run typecheck && npm run lint — with a scratch app/invoices/[id]/page.tsx in place, since reverted; version from package-lock.json

research.claim: notFound() from next/navigation produces a real 404: the built production server answered 404 for an unknown id and 200 for a real one, and the table's draft invoice INV-1004 opened at 200 showing 'Initech Hardware $931.00 2026-11-01 draft'. Every row of the table also gained an href — /invoices/INV-1001 through /invoices/INV-1005 appeared in the list page's HTML.
research.source: ran: npm run start -- --port 3000 then curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' http://localhost:3000/invoices/INV-9999 (404), the same for /invoices/INV-1004 (200), and curl -s http://localhost:3000/invoices | grep -o 'href="/invoices/INV-[0-9]*"'

research.claim: The not-found body does not appear as visible text in the raw HTML: Next streams it inside a hidden <template> Suspense slot, so stripping tags from the curl response yields only the document title. The string is in the response bytes and renders in a browser. A verifier that greps curl output for visible text would wrongly call this missing, which is why the acceptance check says to use a browser — the sandbox is tier 'renders' and drives Chromium.
research.source: ran: curl -s http://localhost:3000/invoices/INV-9999 -o nf2.html && grep -c 'Invoice not found' nf2.html (1 hit, inside the streamed payload, while tag-stripped visible text was only 'Invoices')

research.claim: Diff coverage must reach 80%, and the runner computes it over the changed lines using the DA records in coverage/lcov.info, falling back to whole-file totals only when per-line data is absent. A scratch run with every file in this plan but no test for not-found.tsx measured that file at 0% over 11 lines and would have dragged the change under the minimum; adding the one not-found test brought every new and changed file to 100% line coverage, with total coverage rising from 72.0% to 78.6% over 35 passing tests.
research.source: ran: npm test -- --coverage, read against the diff_min_pct of 80 in .factory/guardrails/coverage.json

research.claim: app/invoices/page.test.tsx and lib/invoices.test.ts are existing test files this change edits, so both are declared. The repo's fourth test file was not in the feature map's list; the committed test files are the four named by git, and tests live beside their source with no tests/ directory.
research.source: ran: git ls-files | grep -E 'test|spec' — app/invoices/export/route.test.ts, app/invoices/page.test.tsx, components/ExportButton.test.tsx, lib/invoices.test.ts

research.claim: Nothing in this plan touches a protected path: .github/workflows/, .factory/bin/, .factory/definition/policy.yaml and .factory/sandbox/ are all out of the change set, and product_work may change code and tests only.
